mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of rising unemployment are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns in periods of declining GDP growth are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in the last two months signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of rising industrial production are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% each over the last two months indicates a strong demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS increase > 5% each in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of rising housing starts and retail sales are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs in the last month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 5-day forward returns in periods of strong payroll growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in the last month signals easing inflationary pressures, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the likelihood of aggressive monetary tightening decreases.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of declining CPI are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% each over the last two months indicates a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending decline.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decrease > 5% each in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns in periods of declining housing starts and retail sales are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
